newsitem.title: CANADA: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

CANADA, July 21 - Montreal - All terminals operating normally with no delays expected. Vancouver - The harbour masters service launch is now available 24 hrs. per day. This will enable vessels requiring ballast water checks prior to discharging ballast during loading operations to be carried out on arrival. In the past this was only during the hours of 0700 hrs. to 1800 hrs. daily. Grain vessels can expect an average wait for a berth from 5 to 7 days. This wait is for Vancouver and Prince Rupert, BC. The new container port at Delta port (Roberts Bank) production is improving and has been reported as at least 20 mph. Coal shipments out of Roberts Bank are heavy this month and delays in the terminal are minimal.

EL SALVADOR - Acajutla - July 21 - Eight vessels due of which 1 vehicles/1 case spare parts, 2 to discharge steel products, 1 each to discharge, milk powder in pallets, butane gas, containers, bulk fertiliser, vehicles. Delays cannot be predicted. 2 Vessels loading at berth of which 1 bulk sugar, 1 full container vessel. 3 Vessels discharging at berth of which 1 corn and soya meal, 1 bulk corn, 1 steel products/general cargo/full containers. 2 Vessels waiting at anchorage to discharge of which 1 corn, 1 bulk wheat.

HONDURAS, July 21 - Puerto Cortes - Vessels berthed, 4 discharging/loading containers, 1 discharging wheat, 1 discharging bagged rice. 4 Vessels awaiting berth to discharge/load containers. Vessels due, 5 to discharge bananas, 8 to load/discharge containers, 1 to discharge urea, 1 to discharge wheat. Puerto Cortes - July 22 - Five vessels berthed of which 2 discharging/loading containers/general, 1 each discharging bagged rice, fertiliser, 1 in ballast. 20 Vessels due of which 2 passenger, 9 to discharge/load containers/general, 6 to discharge/load containers/bananas, 1 to discharge/load generals, 1 to load lumber, 1 to discharge liquid chemicals.

MEXICO, July 22 - Tampico - Vessels in port, 3 general cargo, 1 steel coils, 1 pipes, 1 repair, 1 grain, 1 fuel. Working normally. Altamira - Vessels in port, 2 containers. Working normally. Veracruz - Vessels in port, 1 cars, 3 sugar, 2 containers, 2 general cargo, 2 grain, 3 pipes, 2 oil tankers. Working normally. Manzanillo - Vessels in port, 2 sugar, 1 cement, 2 containers, 2 steel coils, 1 fishmeal. Working normally. Coatzacoalcos - Vessels in port, 9 oil tankers, 10 chemicals, 1 repair. Working normally.

PANAMA, July 19 - Panama Canal - Marine director advised that based on present and projected number of vessels awaiting canal transit and in accordance with rule governing transit reservation system, condition 3 will be in effect at 0001 hours 21/7 continuing until further notice. Reservations previously accepted will be honoured. Restoration of reservations under a less restrictive condition will be reassessed as transit backlog warrants. As of 19/7 the 48 hour backlog was projected at 92 vessels. Available booking slots will be reduced to 8 large (over 91 ft. Beam), and 4 small, daily, and any booked vessel transiting from 21/7 will pay triple the booking fee or have the option to cancel without penalty but then transit as a non-booked vessel. All traffic being delayed approx. 3 days. Projected backlog is 89 vessels as at 0001 hours 21/7. July 21 lock overhauls completed on schedule at 2359 hours 19/7. UNITED STATES, July 21 - Hampton Roads, Va - Four general cargo/container vessels in pier operating, 2 bulkers in pier loading coal, 3 anchored waiting to load. 1 Bulker loading scrap, 2 tankers discharging of which 1 crude oil, 1 uan solution. 1 bulker discharging cement. 2 Vessels in pier under layberth arrangements. Honolulu, HI - Harbour - 6 Vessels berthed of which 2 container, 4 tugs and barges, 1 tanker at anchorage. Barbers Point - Harbour - 2 Barges berthed, 1 tanker at offport moorings.

EAST COAST, Baltimore, MD - No congestion at Dundalk terminal anticipated this week. Clear c/d canal/Baltimore harbour low ceiling. Elevators and coal operations working well with no delays. Average waiting time Consol Coal 3 days. Liquid bulk facilities - Operating normal, no berthing congestion. Anchorage available at Baltimore and Annapolis. Charleston, SC. - No vessels scheduled at shipyard river coal terminal. No delays expected at tanker terminals. All terminals up and running. Columbus Street, North Charleston and Wando terminal will be light. Dredging continues in main channel with no navigation problems. Jacksonville - No heavy berth congestion or delays for the ports of Jacksonville and Fernandina beach, FL. Miami - Traffic expected to be moderate at port of Miami and Port Everglades, no major delays. Passenger terminals available from Tuesday to Thursday. From Friday 0600 hrs to Monday 1900 hrs these terminals are fully operational.

New York, NY - No congestion in New York anchorages. No congestion in tanker terminals and no congestion in sugar terminals. Norfolk, VA - Norfolk southern coal pier expecting 11 vessels during this week. Presently, 2 vessels are anchored waiting to load. Dominion terminal - Expecting 5 vessels. Presently, 1 vessel is anchored waiting to load. Pier IX terminal - Expecting 4 vessels during the next week. Norfolk southern coal pier 6 has undertaken a maintenance period from July 7 to July 28 to perform work on one of the ship loaders. During the period, one loader will be working. At this time, maintenance is ahead of schedule and completion is possible July 25 p.m. or 26 July a.m. Container and general cargo terminals are working normally with no delays. Oil and bulk terminals are all working normally. All channels are opening, with prevailing depths available. Construction is near completion on the work over the Norfolk international terminal, pier 3. Philadelphia, PA - No port congestion in the ports of

GULF COAST, Houston, TX - No congestion at the port of Houston City docks, Houston public grain elevator and Cargill grain elevator. However, congestion exists at Farmland grain elevator, Galveston. Approx. 2-3 days waiting and to some oil/chemical terminals. New Orleans, LA - It is normal for periods of rain to occur during summer season and these conditions cause delays in cargo operation especially grain loading. Grain shipments normal for this season. River stage at 6.6 feet, expected to drop to 5.5 ft. by 24 July. High river conditions will cause delays no ship movement and vessel transit times. Bar pilots advise that the draft for the Mississippi river gulf outlet will be 36 ft. Present max permissible draft at S.W. Pass is 46 ft. Fresh water for vessels under 100,000 dwt 45 ft. Fresh water for vessels over 100,000 dwt. Based on these drafts, all vessels are to maintain sufficient airdraft for transit under bridges in Mississippi river. Some elevators are not working weekends due to slower than

WEST COAST - Columbia river - Grain vessel activity continues to be lower than expected. There are 3 vessels loading and 3 vessels waiting at anchorage. July 28 is an ILWU/Longshore holiday Harry Bridges birthday. This holiday is considered a normal working day with all work being performed at the higher overtime rate. Coos Bay - Vessel traffic slow this past week. One woodchip carrier and one nickel vessel discharging at Glenbrook nickel terminal. This coming week vessel traffic is expected to increase with the arrival of two lumber vessels, one woodchip carrier, 1 nickel discharging vessel and 1 vessel scheduled at Coos Bay dock to load linerboard for China discharge. No delays to vessel traffic due to fog, but as summer progresses fog will cause delays both in the morning and evening. No delays to vessels due to berth congestion or dredging. Honolulu and Barbers Point traffic is light for the upcoming week. Vessel should experience no delays for offport anchorages or inport berths. The ILWU employees

Long Beach and Los Angeles - Pilots strike. The state superior court has granted a temporary restraining order preventing LA pilots from picketing terminals until 24 July at which time the court will re-evaluate status of city/pilot contract negotiations. A federal court has decided not to take this issue under consideration until after superior court has ruled. To date pilots officially are still on strike. However, vessels are moving into/out of the port of Los Angeles with only 2 management pilots causing delays up to 4 hours awaiting a pilot. The ILWU longshoremen are again working the vessels in port of Los Angeles. The port of Long Beach is not affected by the situation at the port of Los Angeles. Port of Long Beach has advised they will not accept any vessel diversions to Long Beach from Los Angeles for discharge due to possibility of the strike situation following such vessels to Long Beach.
